source: Andsager, Beard & Laird (1999), Laboratory Measurements of Axis Ratios for Large Raindrops, Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences 56, 2673-2683
extraction: Table 2, printed p2676, PDF page4; visually checked against rendered page. Table3/Figure4 also visually checked on PDF page6.
choice: Every maximum-fall-distance row, chosen before table extraction. These are measured shape statistics. Table1 velocities and frequencies were not used as observed outcomes.
small_discrepancy: The 4mm mean is 0.808 in Table2 and 0.807 in Table3; both are preserved. Primary score uses Table2 consistently; sensitivity uses Table3. Difference 0.001 is smaller than the reported 0.005 confidence half-width. No digitization of the histogram was needed.
conditions: Deionized water, 25.5m fall. Experiment temperature varied from 8 to 28C; individual run temperatures, local air velocity and full droplet contours unavailable. Nominal comparison uses20C. Size varied within1% per run and2% between runs.
limits: Reported 95% intervals describe measured means, not model or total systematic uncertainty. Several images can belong to one drop. Equilibrium spheroids are compared with time-mean chord ratios of oscillating, potentially non-spheroidal drops; transverse modes and wake locking are omitted.
independence: No previous project study cited this source. Source/table selection and physical model were fixed before table extraction; search previews exposed qualitative findings first. No fitting. Subsequent use for changing the model turns these data into development evidence. This was not a blinded or preregistered validation study.
